rationale.conceptual: The time-dependent tight-binding method is an established but non-trivial technique. It requires careful implementation of Hamiltonian construction in an sp³s* basis, real-time propagation of localized wavefunctions, Fourier analysis, and peak-finding to extract band gaps. The agent must understand the algorithm from the paper and its references, and several components interact, though no novel theoretical derivation is needed.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has 4–6 distinct stages: generate cluster geometries, construct Hamiltonians, propagate wavefunctions for many initial states, compute DOS, and output formatted tables. Dependencies exist (Hamiltonian depends on geometry, propagation on Hamiltonian). The orchestration and numerical implementation (time-stepping, Fourier transforms) are non-trivial but can be performed with standard libraries like NumPy.

difficulty.reasoning: Implementation of a time-dependent tight-binding method for Si nanocrystals: requires building Hamiltonians, time-propagating wavefunctions, and computing DOS; multi-stage pipeline with moderate conceptual complexity.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Largest cluster (35 Å) contains ~1120 Si atoms → 5600 basis functions. Sparse Hamiltonian and wavefunction arrays need ≈3 GB RAM. All parameters are inline; no external dataset. CPU-only propagation across many initial states may take several hours.
